items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I’m thankful that I was fortunate enough to have been reared in that era, even though I was a bystander, I was a listener at the outset of it, and was fortunate enough to be able to hear all of these greats and learn from them.

ctx.x: Oh yes he could play that thing. He used to love that thing. But Ben Webster, that was another case of — I think that we were so blessed to come through the time when we had those people to listen to, to appreciate, and just to make us lose ourselves in what they did. Because they were capable. Ellington — I’d get lost in his beauty, the beauty of the chords, the beauty of the way they and played together, the way they would breathe together, and the sound that they made from Otto Hardwicke to all of the guys.
Oh, Hodges, of course, you know and the baritone player, don’t forget that, he was a baby when he joined the band I understand, from Boston — I can’t think of his name.
